nodes.name: Business design
nodes.what: Describe and maintain Alder's development work and its intended outcomes.
nodes.why: Keep business meaning, authority and guarantees explicit at the source before downstream artifacts rely on a changed decision.
nodes.when: A requester supplies a new objective, or review or research exposes a concrete unresolved business choice or a requested change.
nodes.who: The responsible human designer, assisted by an AI drafting agent; the responsible human confirms business meaning.
nodes.where: The repository's Business Design and associated human review discussion.

nodes.name: Check Item design and confirmation
nodes.what: Optionally derive and review observable expectations from the whole Business Design.
nodes.why: Make requirements review and representative test coverage easier to navigate where the added maintenance is justified.
nodes.when: Business Design and its activity-correlation review are ready, and the task benefits from Check Items or optional Functional Interfaces.
nodes.who: An AI drafts; responsible human designers/requesters review, correct and complete the expectations.
nodes.where: Repository Check list and human review discussion.

nodes.name: Check Items and optional Functional Interfaces
Delivery
nodes.what: Present reviewed changes for human acceptance and publish approved repository changes or releases.
nodes.why: Make the actual scope, evidence and remaining limits reviewable before adoption.
nodes.when: A task is ready for a pull request, or the maintainer explicitly authorizes merge or release after review.
nodes.who: The implementing agent prepares the change; the maintainer authorizes acceptance/release, and the authorized agent or release workflow executes it.
nodes.where: GitHub pull requests and the repository release workflow.

nodes.name: Drift inspection
nodes.what: Optionally detect outdated source/Check/Test relationships and select reconfirmation candidates.
nodes.why: Expose omitted synchronization after source edits without confusing text freshness with business correctness.
nodes.when: A bounded opt-in pilot is in use and its identified source items, Checks or current Test inventory change.
nodes.who: The developer or AI operating the read-only detector and interpreting its candidates.
nodes.where: The optional drift pilot and its supplied fixture/product adapter.

nodes.name: Opt-in source/Check/Test pins and current Test inventory
Fresh review
nodes.what: Independently review the concrete implementation choices against Business Design.
nodes.why: Detect definite mismatches and narrow unresolved business meaning into questions that people can decide.
nodes.when: An implementation or material revision is available for review with its source design and Decisions.
nodes.who: A separate AI reviewer or fresh context; responsible humans decide unresolved business meaning.

nodes.name: Business Graph export
nodes.what: Project an explicitly annotated Business Design into versioned Business Graph JSON.
nodes.why: Make the documented activity/Object correlations machine-readable without creating another authority or maintaining the same meaning twice.
nodes.when: A developer requests a projection or the source design changes and its checked-in example must be regenerated.
nodes.who: The developer or AI invoking the optional export CLI.
nodes.where: Local repository or CI; no network or external service is required.

nodes.name: Implementation
nodes.what: Implement and maintain Alder's guidance, executable tools and tests for the delegated task.
nodes.why: Make the intended work executable or usable and expose concrete choices for subsequent review.
nodes.when: The task has sufficient business direction and technical constraints to proceed; complete prior resolution of every future choice is not required.
nodes.where: An isolated repository branch and local execution environment.

nodes.name: Research evaluation
nodes.what: Evaluate proposed changes to Alder's practices and record whether evidence justifies adoption.
nodes.why: Keep operating guidance grounded in bounded evidence and preserve the distinction between observations and general claims.
nodes.when: A task proposes a practice change or a documented reconsideration condition is met.
nodes.who: The research developer or AI; the maintainer decides adoption of proposed permanent guidance.
nodes.where: Repository research docs and work artifacts.

nodes.name: System design
nodes.what: Choose technical means within Alder's current business intent and task constraints.
nodes.why: Make implementation feasible and reviewable without inventing business policy or prescribing an architecture name.
nodes.when: A development task needs technical choices or new evidence changes an existing technical assumption.
nodes.who: The implementation AI or developer accountable for the delegated technical work.
nodes.where: Repository and task discussion; material choices in Decision Records.

nodes.name: Test design
nodes.what: Plan observable assertions and relevant verification cases for the delegated change.
nodes.why: Verify behavior against the current business intent rather than merely reproducing the implementation's choices.
nodes.when: An implementable change has testable expectations; if Check Items are used, their human review is complete.
nodes.who: The AI or developer responsible for test design.
nodes.where: Repository tests, task plan or existing Check/Test mapping.

nodes.name: Test / verification
nodes.what: Execute relevant tests and gates, and reproduce bounded research observations when the task requires them.
nodes.why: Establish actual implementation evidence and report its limits before a change is delivered.
nodes.when: Implementation changes are ready for verification, or changed expectations require regression testing.
nodes.who: The implementing developer or AI and the configured CI runner.
nodes.where: Local temporary test environments and repository CI.

scope: Develop and maintain Alder's guidance, research evidence and optional tools: define business intent, choose technical means, optionally derive Checks and Test plans, implement, optionally inspect drift, verify, independently review, evaluate research changes and deliver approved changes. Graph export is an optional projection of this design. UI/Viewer design, layout, billing, automatic business approval, mandatory use of optional research practices and permanent Check-to-Code location mappings are outside scope. No product database or production service is operated by this development workflow.
